The Beauty Resistance

By James, Willow, Heidi and Maisie
Scroll
A student communications project

What the beauty industry doesn’t put on the label.

Explore the issues Read the stories
Side effects not included

Our project explores the pressures surrounding modern beauty standards and how they affect both women and men.

  • We will investigate how society, social media and the beauty industry create unrealistic expectations around appearance and how people feel pressure to change themselves to fit these ideals.
  • With a focus on women and traditional beauty standards including expectations around body shape, weight, skin, hair and facial features. Whilst also exploring weight loss injections such as Ozempic and their impact on body image and self esteem.
  • Alongside this we will challenge the idea that body image pressures only affect women by exploring steroid use among men and the pressure to achieve a muscular, lean and “ideal male body”. This will allow us to compare the different ways men and women are encouraged to change themselves in order to meet societal expectations.
  • We aim to question where these standards come from, why people feel pressured to conform, and whether modern society is beginning to resist and redefine what is considered acceptable.

02 · The fine print

Behind every before-and-after is a story the advert doesn’t tell.

Story 01

World Anti-Doping Agency: Natural Is Enough

A social media initiative launched in November 2023 to warn young people about the dangers of non-sport anabolic steroid use.

The WADA partnered with creative agency Redtorch and enlisted seven authentic fitness creators who shared their own body image struggles and insecurities, explaining why they choose natural training over cheating their bodies with steroids.

Like the WADA, we are going to use the internet to spread awareness of the issue to the public by putting QR codes around campus that direct people to our website, where information on our campaign topic can be found.

Source: wada-ama.org: WADA launches Natural Is Enough social media campaign

Story 02

Dove Self-Esteem Project

A global educational initiative launched by the beauty brand Dove in 2004 to help young people build body confidence and positive self-esteem.

Dove replaced traditional professional models in its ads with everyday women of diverse ages, shapes, sizes and ethnicities.

Source: dove.com: Dove Self-Esteem Project

04 · Need to talk?

Support & resources

If anything here feels close to home, you don’t have to deal with it alone. Speak to your GP or someone you trust.

  • NHS Trusted health information on body image, weight-loss medicines and steroid misuse, and how to get help from your GP. nhs.uk
  • FRANK Free, confidential drugs advice, including anabolic steroids. Call 0300 123 6600 or text 82111. talktofrank.com
  • BDD Foundation The UK charity for body dysmorphic disorder, with information and support groups. bddfoundation.org
